message.content: {"letter": "C", "option_text": "Bilateral symmetrical hilar lymphadenopathy with the presence of multiple small peribronchovascular nodules.", "reason": "The chest X-ray demonstrates bilateral hilar prominence and diffuse reticulonodular opacities, which are classic radiographic features of pulmonary sarcoidosis (Stage II). Option C accurately describes this pattern of bilateral symmetrical hilar lymphadenopathy combined with peribronchovascular nodules. In contrast, options describing cavitation (A), unilateral masses (B, D, E), or isolated ground glass opacities (F) are more suggestive of tuberculosis, lymphoma, or other interstitial lung diseases rather than the typical presentation of sarcoidosis seen here."}
